applies_to: Pressure-independent and pressure-dependent VAV boxes and zone dampers controlled by the AAON VAV/Zone BACnet controller.
summary: The VAVZB is AAON's VAV box and zone damper controller, used on AAON VAV and zoning systems with an AAON unit controller. It has an on-board BACnet MS/TP port next to the AAON communication loop. Over BACnet it exposes 11 analog inputs, 24 setpoint and configuration analog values, 17 binary status and alarm inputs and 3 multi-state status inputs.
notes: The guide has no read/write column; AVs are shown as writable (they carry limit ranges) and AI/BI/MI as read-only.
The BACnet map has no occupancy command or BAS sensor input; occupancy comes over the AAON communication loop from the unit controller or a GPC-XP.
Units are not printed for the inputs; temperature units here follow the °F limit ranges. Damper/airflow settings (0-30000) are damper % or CFM depending on box type.
BI 13 and BI 14 are the damper opening and closing alarms; BI 15-17 and BI 11-12 match the alarms listed in the sequence of operation.
Airflow points only apply to pressure-independent boxes; fan and heat points only with the expansion module.

source.title: VAV/Zone BACnet Controller Package Technical Guide (Appendix B: BACnet MS/TP Parameters)

integration.summary: Set the MAC address, device ID and MS/TP baud on the controller's LCD Settings screens. The BMS can then read zone temperature, airflow, damper position and alarms and write the occupied heating and cooling setpoints and damper/airflow limits. Occupancy itself still comes from the AAON unit controller or GPC-XP over the AAON communication loop.

integration.enable: There is no BACnet occupancy or enable point. The VAVZB takes its occupied/unoccupied command from the AAON unit controller or a GPC-XP over the AAON communication loop, and push-button overrides on the room sensor return it to occupied for 0-8 hours (AV 8). Damper force modes (including AV 21 Force Damper to Fixed Position) stay active until cancelled or power is removed.
setup: BACnet MAC address 0-127, default 1; set on the LCD Settings screen.
Device ID up to 7 digits, set on the LCD (the example screen shows 15000); no default is stated.
The AAON loop address (Unit ID 1-58) is separate from the BACnet MAC address.
gotchas: The guide gives no read/write column; test writes to the AVs before relying on them.
BACnet has no occupancy command; MI 1 state 7 shows when the box has lost communication with the RTU.
Damper/airflow settings mean % or CFM depending on whether the box is pressure-independent.
